entries.title: Deterministic rule engine over an LLM classifier
entries.problem: A message router has to assign action + type + reason. An LLM classifier is the obvious default in 2026.
entries.root_cause: Three properties of the data made the LLM the worse fit, none of them obvious before measuring.
entries.chosen: Three-tier deterministic rule engine: SAFETY > RELATIONSHIP/URGENCY > ENGAGEMENT > DEFAULT
rejected: LLM classifier over raw message text
entries.evidence: (1) Labeled reasons were templated: 24 distinct strings across 30 rows -- ground truth states which RULE fired, not what the text said. (2) One labeled row was a prompt-injection attack whose correct label was mute/scam; a rule engine is structurally immune because message text never enters a decision prompt. (3) Every safety-critical signal was a structured field, not prose.

benchmarks.note: templated => rule identity is the label

entries.blast_radius: Whole system. Every downstream decision inherits determinism.
entries.impact: One output hash across 5 processes x 5 PYTHONHASHSEED values
entries.reconsider_if: Reasons in the graded set turn out to be free-form prose rather than templates, OR the type taxonomy grows past what ~40 rules can express without collisions.
entries.lesson: Read the LABELS before choosing the model. The label format tells you what is actually being scored.

entries.title: Dynamic confidence lost to a constant
entries.problem: More matched signals 'should' mean higher confidence.
entries.root_cause: Intuition substituted for measurement.
entries.chosen: Static per-rule confidence; the dynamic function was DELETED
entries.evidence: Also emitted values above the observed label band on 3/30 rows.

benchmarks.note: dynamic worse on every action subset

entries.blast_radius: 0 rows changed action or type; confidence column only.
entries.reconsider_if: Labeled confidences ever show >0.15 spread WITHIN a single rule -- that would mean the label depends on the message, not the rule.
entries.lesson: Disabling is not enough. Delete. Disabled code is a future accident.

entries.title: KeyError ran before the row-level exception handler
entries.problem: A single malformed row produced zero output rows.
entries.root_cause: The try/except was placed inside the loop body, below the dictionary access that raised.
entries.chosen: Guarded access above the handler; per-row isolation
entries.evidence: Injected one missing column -> 0 rows written, exit 0. Silent.
entries.blast_radius: Total. A graded run would have scored zero.
entries.lesson: Test the failure path by injecting the failure, not by reading the code.

entries.title: BOM / invalid UTF-8 aborted the whole load
entries.problem: Strict decoding on the input CSV.
entries.root_cause: Default encoding assumptions on a file supplied by someone else.
entries.chosen: utf-8-sig with errors='replace'
entries.evidence: A UTF-8 BOM is what Excel writes by default.
entries.blast_radius: Total, conditional on the grader's file encoding.
entries.lesson: You do not control the encoding of an input you are handed.

entries.title: Media paths resolved from the working directory, not the dataset dir
entries.problem: Every media file failed to open, and the failure was swallowed.
entries.root_cause: Relative path resolution plus a bare except.
entries.chosen: Resolve media relative to the dataset root; log every miss
entries.evidence: FileNotFoundError caught and discarded on 100% of media rows.

benchmarks.metric: media files opened when run from repo root

entries.blast_radius: All 33 media rows silently degraded to text-only.
entries.lesson: A swallowed exception turns a total failure into a plausible result.

entries.title: Vision output universally truncated mid-word
entries.problem: Every caption came back 44-71 characters and cut off.
entries.root_cause: Thinking tokens were billed against the same output budget as the visible response.
entries.chosen: Raise the output budget above the reasoning allocation
entries.blast_radius: All image rows.
entries.lesson: A uniform output length is a budget symptom, not a content property.

entries.title: SELF-INFLICTED: a distress rule promoted a real-estate robocall
entries.problem: A marketing call naming a hospital routed to notify/urgent.
entries.root_cause: Location nouns sat in a distress lexicon -- but the REAL root cause was methodological: blast radius was measured with speech disabled, then shipped with speech enabled.
entries.chosen: Remove location nouns; re-measure blast radius in the shipped configuration

benchmarks.metric: rows regressed by the change as shipped
benchmarks.note: the measurement was taken in the wrong configuration

entries.blast_radius: 1 graded row -- invisible to the harness that approved it.
entries.reconsider_if: Never. The lexicon fix stands; the lesson is about method.
entries.lesson: Measure in the configuration you SHIP. A blast radius computed with a component disabled is not a blast radius.

entries.title: The fix disabled itself: de-obfuscation destroyed word boundaries
entries.problem: Spaced-out evasions like 'Share the O T P now' bypassed detection.
entries.root_cause: The de-obfuscator stripped ALL whitespace, collapsing the text to 'SharetheOTPnow' -- which no longer matches the word-boundary pattern the rule needs.
entries.chosen: Collapse only intra-token spacing; preserve word boundaries
entries.blast_radius: 0 rows on the sample corpus; 5 on the attack battery.
entries.lesson: A fix that defeats the mechanism it feeds is worse than no fix -- it looks like coverage.

entries.title: Two rules encoded opposite policies for the same message
entries.problem: 'Ma is in ICU, send money to this UPI' routed to notify.
entries.root_cause: A distress rule and a payment-scam rule both matched; tier order let distress win.
entries.chosen: DELETE the distress-escalation rule. Patching its condition would have made it dead code.
rejected: add an exception clause to the distress rule
entries.evidence: After deletion the row routes mute/scam. No other row changed.
entries.blast_radius: 1 row changed, 109 identical.
entries.lesson: When a rule needs an exception for the case that matters, the rule is wrong, not incomplete.

entries.title: 'The images carry no signal' was a conclusion about two vendors
entries.problem: Hosted vision extracted 0 characters on 15/15 image rows, and that was recorded as a property of the corpus.
entries.root_cause: Confusing the behaviour of a remote service with the content of the data.
entries.chosen: Local OCR engine (RapidOCR), made the default vision provider
rejected: accepting that the images were blank
entries.evidence: 7/7 pixel-only scams caught with OCR on; 7/7 escape with it off.
entries.blast_radius: 0 of 110 output rows changed -- the channel is live and redundant on THIS corpus.
entries.reconsider_if: A corpus where image text is the sole safety signal on rows the rules do not already catch.
entries.lesson: When a component returns nothing, prove WHERE the nothing came from.

entries.title: Image MIME type guessed from the filename extension
entries.problem: Uploads declared image/jpeg for PNG, WebP and AVIF payloads.
entries.root_cause: Extensions in the corpus were deliberately wrong.
entries.chosen: Sniff magic bytes; fall back to extension only when bytes are inconclusive
entries.blast_radius: 19 of 33 media files were being mislabeled on the wire.
entries.lesson: A filename is a hint from an untrusted party.

entries.title: Audio MIME guessed from the filename -- same class, other modality
entries.problem: WAV and M4A payloads declared as audio/mpeg.
entries.root_cause: The image fix was applied to images only.
entries.chosen: Shared byte-sniffing helper across both modalities
entries.blast_radius: 9 of 13 audio uploads.
entries.lesson: When you find a class of bug, grep for the class -- not the instance.

entries.title: Image text may escalate safety but must not redefine intent
entries.problem: Enabling OCR regressed two rows from urgent to event.
entries.root_cause: An unrelated calendar screenshot and a generic brochure tripped intent lexicons. A poster is authored by a THIRD PARTY; it should not redefine what the sender meant.
entries.chosen: Scope image text to the SAFETY tier only. Voice participates fully, because the transcript IS the message.
entries.evidence: Spec-grounded asymmetry: message_text is empty on 8/8 voice rows and non-empty on 15/15 image rows.
entries.blast_radius: Turned enabling OCR into a zero-regression change.
entries.reconsider_if: A dataset where images ARE the message -- e.g. rows with empty message_text and an image attachment.
entries.lesson: Untrusted content may escalate safety. It must never redefine intent.

entries.title: Ablation harness measured nothing and reported a clean zero
entries.problem: Media ablation reported '0 of 110 rows changed'.
entries.root_cause: It monkeypatched a module attribute, but the consumer had bound that name into its own namespace at import time. BOTH ARMS ran the null backend.
entries.chosen: Inject through the supported parameter seam
entries.blast_radius: Would have shipped a false 'media is useless' conclusion into the writeup.
entries.lesson: A clean zero from a broken harness is the most dangerous result in engineering, because it confirms what you already believed.

entries.title: Reachability prober reported 3 dead rules and 7 shadowed -- all false
entries.problem: A rule-coverage audit claimed dead code in the safety tier.
entries.root_cause: It randomised only fields matching a naming prefix (23 of 37 booleans) and returned the FIRST matching condition, so a tier-1 rule won nearly every draw.
entries.chosen: Search the full feature space; require the rule ITSELF to win
entries.blast_radius: Would have deleted reachable safety rules.
entries.lesson: Distinguish 'unsatisfiable' from 'never won a random draw'.

entries.title: Label-leakage audit fired a BLOCKER on a healthy repository
entries.problem: A confident release blocker on a repo with no leakage.
entries.root_cause: Three bugs at once: it scanned root exploratory scripts as production, matched synthetic fixture variables as dataset ids, and treated docstrings as executable code.
entries.chosen: AST docstring stripping, production-glob scoping, assignment exclusion. Postmortem preserved in the module docstring.
entries.evidence: A fourth bug surfaced alongside: Engineering Memory attached 'dense retrieval' as prior art to 'dataset ids in code' on the single shared word 'evidence'. Fixed with a recall floor.
entries.blast_radius: Would have blocked a correct release.
entries.lesson: Your audit tooling needs a negative control as much as your model does.

entries.title: Catastrophic regex backtracking on adversarial input
entries.problem: A single 40 KB message took 40.3 seconds to route.
entries.root_cause: An unbounded quantifier on a domain-label pattern.
entries.chosen: Bound the quantifier to RFC 1035's 63-octet DNS label limit
entries.blast_radius: 0 rows changed. Denial-of-service path closed.
entries.lesson: Bound every quantifier with a real-world standard, not a guess -- then the bound is defensible under questioning.

entries.title: LLM arbitration was silently ON whenever any key was present
entries.problem: A network call and raw message text entered a prompt on 6/110 rows without any explicit opt-in.
entries.root_cause: Feature-gated on credential presence rather than on intent.
entries.chosen: Explicit ARBITRATION=on opt-in; default off
entries.evidence: On the labeled rows where it could fire, the deterministic verdict was already correct, and escalation was its only possible action -- every intervention it could make there was a guaranteed regression.
entries.blast_radius: 6 of 110 rows eligible; 0 improved.
entries.reconsider_if: A row class appears where the deterministic tiers genuinely tie and the tie is resolvable from prose.
entries.lesson: A capability gated on credential presence is a capability with no off switch.

entries.title: Bare `pytest` aborted the entire suite
entries.problem: 63 passing tests displayed as a red, interrupted run.
entries.root_cause: A stale exploratory script named test_*.py at the repo root made API calls at import time, during collection.
entries.chosen: Scope collection with testpaths
entries.blast_radius: The first command a reviewer types.
entries.lesson: Run the command a REVIEWER runs first, not the one you run.

entries.title: The suite passed only by accident of alphabetical import order
entries.problem: One test file, run alone, failed with ModuleNotFoundError.
entries.root_cause: An earlier-sorting file performed a sys.path insert at import.
entries.chosen: Declare pythonpath in configuration
entries.evidence: Every file now passes in isolation.
entries.blast_radius: Renaming any test file would have broken every other.
entries.lesson: Run each test file alone in CI, not only the suite.

entries.title: A determinism test asserted that a hosted service is bit-stable
entries.problem: Intermittent failure on one row.
entries.root_cause: The test called the pipeline twice with credentials present, making two live ASR requests, and asserted equality.
entries.chosen: Autouse fixture clearing all credentials -- hermetic by default

benchmarks.note: a dozen hidden live calls stopped

entries.blast_radius: The suite now measures this system, not someone else's uptime.
entries.lesson: If a test needs the network, it is testing the network.

entries.title: A performance benchmark overwrote the submission artifact
entries.problem: output.csv silently reverted to a degraded configuration.
entries.root_cause: The benchmark invoked the CLI without an output flag, three times per run, writing to the real artifact path.
entries.chosen: Benchmarks write to a temp path; a regression test asserts the artifact is untouched
entries.evidence: A correctly-classified scam reverted to benign between runs.
entries.blast_radius: Artifact corruption invisible in any file listing.
entries.lesson: An audit must never mutate what it audits.

entries.title: A marketing unsubscribe footer was not treated as promotional
entries.problem: The last remaining labeled miss.
entries.root_cause: The promotional lexicon covered offer language but not the regulatory footer that legally accompanies bulk marketing.
entries.chosen: Add the unsubscribe footer as a promotional signal, explicitly excluding the near-identical phrase that scams mimic
entries.blast_radius: 1 graded row -- whose text is byte-identical to a labeled row carrying that exact answer.
entries.lesson: A good late fix keys on a REGULATORY invariant, not on a phrasing, and states its blast radius in rows.

entries.title: Similarity metric structurally preferred short boilerplate
entries.problem: Correct evidence ranked 6th of 21 candidates.
entries.root_cause: The overlap coefficient divides by min(|a|,|b|), so a short document sharing generic terms outranks a longer one sharing distinctive terms.
entries.chosen: BM25 with canonical k1=1.5, b=0.75 -- deliberately untuned

benchmarks.note: truth shared 6 distinctive terms over 18 tokens; five near-duplicate 10-token messages scored 0.600 each

entries.blast_radius: 24 of 110 evidence cells re-ranked; action and type unchanged.
entries.reconsider_if: A labeled evidence set large enough (>200 rows) that tuning k1/b would not simply overfit.
entries.lesson: Aggregate gain is weak evidence. A diagnosed MECHANISM is strong.

entries.title: Mention detection assumed the SHAPE of a user id
entries.problem: Rules depending on @-mentions were silently dead under renamed ids.
entries.root_cause: It harvested tokens matching a regex for the sample's id convention, then compared to the real id. The comparison was principled; the harvest was not.
entries.chosen: Search for '@' followed by the ACTUAL recipient id -- format-agnostic
entries.blast_radius: 0 rows on this dataset. Removes a hidden-data failure mode.
entries.lesson: Never encode the shape of an identifier someone else generates.

entries.title: History ordered by raw string sort of timestamps
entries.problem: Chronological only for zero-padded, most-significant-first dates.
entries.root_cause: The spec fixes no timestamp format; the sample happened to be ISO.
entries.chosen: Format-agnostic sort key, falling back to lexical when ambiguous
entries.evidence: Day-first dates produced different output before the fix.
entries.blast_radius: 0 rows on this dataset.
entries.lesson: 'The sample happened to be X' is the definition of coupling.

entries.title: A lexicon term was copied verbatim from one sample sentence
entries.problem: The term fired on exactly 1 of 537 corpus texts.
entries.root_cause: Transcribed to make one message classify, rather than to express the category.
entries.chosen: Express the semantic category, guarded by transport context

benchmarks.metric: corpus texts matched by the copied term
benchmarks.note: a match count of exactly 1 is the smell

entries.blast_radius: 0 rows changed; strictly broader and safer.
entries.lesson: Count how many rows each lexicon term matches. Exactly one is a smell.

entries.title: Local OCR cost 0.25s -> 45s and 7 MB -> 500 MB of heap
entries.problem: Making OCR the default provider made the run 180x slower.
entries.root_cause: A local detection+recognition model loads into the process.
entries.chosen: Ship it anyway, and DOCUMENT the trade rather than hiding it
entries.blast_radius: 0 output rows. Pure cost.
entries.reconsider_if: A submission with a wall-clock or memory limit. Then the correct move is documented degradation, not silent removal.
entries.lesson: Document the trade you made. A hidden 180x is a defect; a stated 180x is a decision.

entries.title: Dense embeddings / RRF / cross-encoder for evidence retrieval
entries.problem: Lexical retrieval looks unsophisticated next to embeddings.
entries.root_cause: The relation being scored is topical word OVERLAP, not paraphrase. Bi-encoders are built for the thing that is not being asked.
entries.chosen: BM25 over a rule-scoped candidate pool

benchmarks.metric: configs dominating the shipped one on all 6 metrics

entries.blast_radius: None shipped.
entries.reconsider_if: The evidence relation becomes paraphrase-based -- e.g. graded evidence that shares NO tokens with the query. Test for this by measuring token overlap between query and gold evidence; if median overlap drops below 2 terms, re-open.
entries.lesson: Benchmark the fashionable option. Publish the number when it loses.

entries.title: Widen the evidence candidate pool to all user history
entries.problem: Rule-scoped pools cap recall at 83.9%.
entries.root_cause: Extra candidates cost more precision than the recovered recall is worth.
entries.chosen: Keep rule-scoped pools
entries.blast_radius: None shipped.
entries.reconsider_if: Scoring changes from set-F1 to recall-at-k, where a higher ceiling would actually pay.
entries.lesson: A higher CEILING is not a higher score. Measure the metric you are graded on.

entries.title: Temporal / metadata / behaviour re-ranking of evidence
entries.problem: Recency and sender-relationship 'obviously' matter for relevance.
entries.root_cause: The signals are constant or near-constant within a candidate pool, so they reorder nothing.
entries.chosen: Pure BM25

benchmarks.note: byte-identical output across every weighting tried

entries.blast_radius: None shipped. Literally zero bytes changed.
entries.reconsider_if: Candidate pools become heterogeneous in time -- e.g. pools spanning months rather than one conversation.
entries.lesson: A signal that is constant within the comparison set carries no information, however predictive it is globally.

entries.title: Per-user quiet-hours personalisation
entries.problem: Routing 'should' respect when a user actually reads messages.
entries.root_cause: No association exists in the data between hour-of-day and the labeled action.
entries.chosen: No temporal personalisation

benchmarks.note: not weak -- zero to three decimals

entries.blast_radius: None shipped.
entries.reconsider_if: A dataset that includes per-user read receipts or notification-dismissal events. The signal is absent here, not merely weak.
entries.lesson: Measure the association before building the feature. Cramer's V costs ten lines.

entries.title: Recalibrate confidence to reduce Expected Calibration Error
entries.problem: ECE measured 0.138 -- systematically under-confident.
entries.root_cause: ECE was the wrong objective. The LABELS are deliberately under-confident, so calibrating to correctness moves away from the thing being scored.
entries.chosen: Match the labeling policy, not textbook calibration

benchmarks.note: the labels are worse-calibrated than we are

benchmarks.metric: MAE under the best ECE-improving shift

entries.blast_radius: None shipped.
entries.reconsider_if: A rubric that scores calibration directly rather than scoring distance to a labeled confidence value.
entries.lesson: Calibrate to the TARGET, not to an ideal. Measure the ground truth's own calibration first.

entries.title: A visual model beyond OCR
entries.problem: Judges may reject submissions that only run OCR.
entries.root_cause: No headroom. The rows a visual signal could reach are already correct, or unreachable by any pixel.
entries.chosen: OCR only, scoped to the safety tier

benchmarks.metric: graded image rows decided without reading media

benchmarks.note: and it FAILS on the single image it would exist for

entries.blast_radius: None shipped.
entries.reconsider_if: Rows appear where message_text is empty AND the image is not text-bearing -- a photograph carrying the whole meaning.
entries.lesson: Build the STRONGEST version of the idea before rejecting it. '19/20 and wrong on the one that matters' is a real answer; 'I didn't try' is not.

entries.title: Replace hosted ASR with local Whisper
entries.problem: Hosted ASR forfeits determinism and requires a key.
entries.root_cause: Local transcription loses the exact entity the safety rules key on.
entries.chosen: Hosted whisper-large-v3, with a documented determinism boundary

benchmarks.note: a TIE -- the aggregate is blind to this
one substituted consonant flips a graded row

entries.blast_radius: None shipped.
entries.reconsider_if: A local model whose entity-level accuracy on credential terms is verified, OR a submission that forbids network calls -- in which case ship local AND state the degradation.
entries.lesson: An aggregate score can be completely blind to the failure that matters. Probe entities, not averages.

entries.title: Cap evidence at k=1 or k=2 instead of the shipped policy
entries.problem: Fewer citations might raise precision.
entries.root_cause: The metrics disagree with each other and the confidence intervals overlap -- there is no measurement that decides it.
entries.chosen: Keep the shipped cap

benchmarks.note: Wilson CIs overlap for every pair

entries.blast_radius: None shipped.
entries.reconsider_if: A labeled evidence set large enough for the intervals to separate. At n=28 no cap is distinguishable.
entries.lesson: 'The measurement does not decide it' is a legitimate result. Do not manufacture a winner from noise.

entries.title: Dynamic per-message confidence scaling
entries.problem: More matched signals 'should' mean higher confidence.
entries.root_cause: Intuition, not measurement.
entries.chosen: Static per-rule confidence
entries.blast_radius: None shipped.
entries.reconsider_if: Labeled confidence varies by more than 0.15 within a single rule's rows.
entries.lesson: The decision record and the finding are separate artifacts: one says what happened, the other says what not to re-propose.

entries.title: Pin the output hash, and keep a RE-PIN LOG
entries.problem: Any change can silently alter 110 rows.
entries.root_cause: Without a pin, a regression is invisible until scoring.
entries.chosen: A test asserting one sha256 over the full output, plus a log recording every re-pin with its cause, effect and score delta
entries.evidence: The re-pin log is the artifact: it turns 'the hash changed' into 'the hash changed because F-41 fixed the last labeled miss, 29/30 -> 30/30'.
entries.blast_radius: Every subsequent change.
entries.lesson: A pinned hash without a re-pin log trains you to update the pin reflexively. The log is what makes the pin mean something.

entries.title: Every constant carries a provenance tag
entries.problem: An interviewer asked for a retrieval hyperparameter and it could not be recalled.
entries.root_cause: Constants had values but no recorded justification.
entries.chosen: CONSTANTS.md with a provenance column: MEASURED / SPEC / STANDARD / BOUND / JUDGEMENT
entries.evidence: STANDARD is the load-bearing tag: 'k1=1.5, b=0.75 are the canonical Robertson/Sparck Jones defaults and I deliberately did NOT tune them' is stronger than a fabricated sweep, and survives the follow-up 'show me the sweep'.
entries.blast_radius: Documentation only. Zero code change.
entries.lesson: Owning a number means knowing where it came from -- including 'I took the standard value on purpose'.

entries.title: Tests clear credentials by default
entries.problem: Tests behaved differently depending on the operator's environment.
entries.root_cause: Any test that can reach the network eventually does.
entries.chosen: An autouse fixture that pops every known API key variable
entries.blast_radius: Whole suite. Network-dependent tests must now opt in explicitly.
entries.lesson: Make the safe configuration the default, not the documented one.
